EDGE-pos1.label: violation
EDGE-pos1.note: The use case takes a retry limit from the permits adapter package through its index barrel.

EDGE-pos2.label: violation
EDGE-pos2.note: The use case loads the permit service's SDK with a dynamic import() to check a permit number before booking.

EDGE-pos3.label: violation
EDGE-pos3.note: The core permit clearance types a field with an inline type import of the permit service's response type.

EDGE-pos4.label: violation
EDGE-pos4.note: The permit gateway moves to src/application/adapters/; the folder is named adapters but the spec puts it in the application layer, and the file imports the SDK.

EDGE-twin1.label: clean
EDGE-twin1.note: The composition root imports the outbound adapters through an index barrel in src/adapters/out; config may depend on adapters.

EDGE-twin2.label: clean
EDGE-twin2.note: The permit gateway moves to src/integrations/icetrail/; the spec adds src/integrations/** to the outbound adapter layer, so the SDK import is an adapter's.

KEY-pos1.label: violation
KEY-pos1.note: The webhook passes the raw hazard band; the use case looks it up in a Record keyed by the bulletin service's band words.

KEY-pos2.label: violation
KEY-pos2.note: The permit port carries the raw permit state; a domain function decides the outcome with an === chain over the permit service's state words.

KEY-twin1.label: clean
KEY-twin1.note: Same band table as KEY-pos1, but it sits in the webhook adapter, which hands the core its own route condition.

KEY-twin2.label: clean
KEY-twin2.note: The domain adds a notice-hours table keyed by the company's own route condition words.

KEY-twin3.label: clean
KEY-twin3.note: Same band table and raw band as KEY-pos1, but the spec glossary declares the five band words as the company's own hazard scale.

SET-pos1.label: violation
SET-pos1.note: The webhook hands the raw hazard band to the core; the domain copies the bulletin service's five bands as a union and the use case casts the port's text to it.

SET-pos2.label: violation
SET-pos2.note: The permit port carries the permit service's raw permit state; the domain copies its six states as a const array and the use case casts the port's text to it.

SET-twin1.label: clean
SET-twin1.note: The core adds its own permit progress set (submitted, in-review, granted, withdrawn), mapped from the six vendor states in the gateway.

SET-twin2.label: clean
SET-twin2.note: The guide logs their own sky reading (CALM, GUSTY, WHITEOUT) through the HTTP adapter; it shares one word of five with the bulletin service's bands by coincidence.

WORD-pos1.label: violation
WORD-pos1.note: The core permit clearance gains a field named warden, the permit service's own field name for the ranger on duty.

WORD-pos2.label: violation
WORD-pos2.note: The core booking status replaces its own ON_HOLD with DEFERRED, a value word of the permit service's permit states.

WORD-twin1.label: clean
WORD-twin1.note: The company adds its own guide quota (most clients one guide may lead), declared in the spec glossary; the permit service also has a field quota.

WORD-twin2.label: clean
WORD-twin2.note: The booking gains the client's free-text notes; notes is a generic word that the permit service also uses for its own free text.
